cards.title: Choose a Shopping bid strategy based on account conversion data
cards.summary: Start a new Shopping campaign on Maximize Clicks, then graduate to Maximize Conversion Value and target ROAS as conversions accumulate.
cards.use_when: You are setting the bidding strategy for a Shopping campaign and need to decide between clicks and conversion-based bidding.

cards.title: Configure Shopping targeting: presence only, no search partners
cards.summary: Set geo targeting to presence-only, uncheck search network, and use all devices to keep Shopping spend on real in-market buyers.
cards.use_when: You are finalizing locations, networks and devices on a Shopping campaign.

cards.title: Exclude branded searches from a non-branded Shopping campaign
cards.summary: Add your brand name variations as exact-match negative keywords so your prospecting Shopping campaign stays non-branded.
cards.use_when: You run a Shopping campaign intended for new-customer, non-brand acquisition and want branded traffic excluded.

cards.title: Sequence a second all-products Shopping campaign after bestsellers prove out
cards.summary: Once bestsellers deliver consistent sales and ROAS, launch an all-products Shopping campaign with no exclusions to find the next winners.
cards.use_when: Your bestsellers Shopping campaign is producing consistent sales and you want to prospect for additional high-performing products.

cards.title: Prune underperforming products from a bestsellers campaign
cards.summary: Exclude products from the bestsellers campaign that received meaningful spend and clicks but failed to perform.
cards.use_when: A bestsellers Shopping campaign is live and some products are dragging down overall ROAS.

cards.title: Add a low-budget branded Shopping campaign to capture branded product searches
cards.summary: If you have significant branded demand, run an all-products Shopping campaign with a brand-negative script at a small budget to show products for brand searches.
cards.use_when: You have meaningful branded search volume (from ads, organic or other channels) and are not fully capturing it with search campaigns.

cards.title: Check audience lists and tagging before any remarketing campaign
cards.summary: Ensure the Google Ads tag, GA4 and linked accounts are feeding audience lists, and wait until lists are large enough to target.
cards.use_when: You plan to run any display, video or PMAX remarketing campaign and need working audience data first.

cards.title: Set up a Display remarketing campaign for returning visitors
cards.summary: Build a low-budget Display campaign targeting all-site visitors with conversion-value bidding and strictly non-expanded targeting.
cards.use_when: You have re-engagement audiences populated and want to retarget past site visitors with Display image ads.

cards.title: Run Video remarketing for site visitors with a product feed attached
cards.summary: Set up a YouTube video remarketing campaign using conversion bidding, tight site-visitor audiences, 3/day frequency cap, and product feed relevance.
cards.use_when: You want a more efficient remarketing channel than Display and are ready to retarget site visitors via YouTube.

cards.title: Use 2-3 high-quality ad copy assets rather than filling every field
cards.summary: Write fewer, stronger headlines and descriptions in remarketing ads instead of padding out every asset suggestion.
cards.use_when: You are building a Display or Video remarketing ad and Google offers many headline/description slots.

cards.title: Position PMAX as a remarketing weapon alongside new-customer Shopping
cards.summary: Use PMAX to retarget Shopping customers with product listings, keeping Shopping as the new-customer acquisition funnel.
cards.use_when: You already have Shopping campaigns acquiring new customers and want a retargeting layer using PMAX.

cards.title: Feed-Only Performance Max Alongside Standard Shopping
cards.summary: Test a feed-led retail PMax configuration against the store baseline without assuming strict audience or channel isolation.
cards.use_when: Evaluating a feed-led versus full-asset Performance Max campaign for an ecommerce product catalog.

cards.title: Excluding Branded Traffic from PMAX to Protect Attribution
cards.summary: Build a negative keyword list of brand terms and apply it to PMAX so brand demand stays in branded Shopping and Search campaigns and PMAX only handles non-branded remarketing.
cards.use_when: Merchandising/measurement decision when PMAX is absorbing branded searches and inflating its apparent results while muddying which campaign actually drives new customers.

cards.title: Deciding Between Feed-Only PMAX and Asset-Filled PMAX
cards.summary: Test a feed-led retail PMax configuration against the store baseline without assuming strict audience or channel isolation.
cards.use_when: Evaluating a feed-led versus full-asset Performance Max campaign for an ecommerce product catalog.

cards.title: Budgeting and Sequencing Demand Gen Campaigns
cards.summary: Sequence Demand Gen as the top-of-funnel step after PMAX, and allocate on the order of 30% of account budget when new-customer acquisition is the priority.
cards.use_when: Budget and rollout planning for a store deciding when to add Demand Gen and how much daily spend to commit relative to its existing Shopping/PMAX setup.

cards.title: Demand Gen Setup: Settings, Placements and Device Controls
cards.summary: Configure Demand Gen location, device and partner settings to keep spend on higher-quality placements and, where desired, bias video delivery toward Shorts.
cards.use_when: Technical setup of a Demand Gen campaign for a store that wants control over placement quality and format, especially when repurposing short-form social creatives.

cards.title: Structuring Demand Gen Ad Groups by Creative Theme
cards.summary: Split Demand Gen ad groups by creative theme (e.g. UGC product reviews) and keep image and product creatives in separate ad groups or campaigns for clean testing.
cards.use_when: Creative and ad-group planning when launching Demand Gen for a store that has multiple creative concepts or formats to test against a product set.

cards.title: Keeping Demand Gen Assets Few and Varied Enough to Test
cards.summary: Limit headlines/descriptions to one to three high-quality options per ad so split tests remain interpretable instead of exploding into untraceable combinations.
cards.use_when: Creative testing decision for a store setting up Demand Gen (or similar) ads that wants to know which messaging actually drives conversions.

cards.title: Audience Signals in Demand Gen: Bias Toward Cold Reach
cards.summary: Leave Demand Gen targeting open or use a few in-market/search-theme signals, but never import your own customer or remarketing lists, which pushes it toward warm traffic.
cards.use_when: Targeting setup for a Demand Gen campaign when the goal is new-customer acquisition and you must avoid duplicating remarketing already handled by PMAX.

cards.title: Assigning Funnel Roles Across the Google Ads Account
cards.summary: Map each campaign type to a funnel job — Shopping/Search for new and branded demand, Display/YouTube for remarketing, PMAX for product remarketing, Demand Gen for top-of-funnel cold reach.
cards.use_when: Whole-account architecture review for a store unsure whether campaigns are duplicating work, cannibalizing each other, or leaving a funnel stage uncovered.

cards.title: Pre-Launch Checklist for Google Ads Campaign Settings
cards.summary: A short checklist of settings the source disables or verifies across PMAX and Demand Gen: auto-created assets, video enhancements, optimized targeting, video partners and video format coverage.
cards.use_when: Final QA before launching or editing a PMAX or Demand Gen campaign in a store's account, to avoid giving Google uncontrolled creative and placement decisions.

cards.title: Pre-diagnosis rules: change history, time horizon, conversion latency
cards.summary: Three checks to run before touching a Google Ads account that looks like it's underperforming.
cards.use_when: Before diagnosing or editing Google Ads when a store's revenue or ROAS appears to have dropped.

cards.title: Level-one business check: cross-channel spend weighting and the revenue equation
cards.summary: Determine whether a revenue dip is even a Google problem by checking media mix share and which revenue-equation lever moved.
cards.use_when: When a store reports a revenue or efficiency drop and you must decide whether to investigate Google Ads, Meta/other channels, or the website first.

cards.title: Check seasonality against a forecast before diagnosing
cards.summary: Use forecasting to rule out expected seasonal dips so you don't run a multi-hour diagnostic on normal fluctuation.
cards.use_when: When a store's revenue dips and you need to decide whether the decline is a real anomaly or expected seasonality before investing time in root-cause work.

cards.title: Prioritise diagnosis by spend: top-5 campaigns only
cards.summary: Ignore low-spend campaigns during diagnosis because even a doubled result there cannot move the business.
cards.use_when: When drilling into a Google Ads account to find the cause of a material business decline.

cards.title: 90–180 day weekly overview scan before drilling into campaigns
cards.summary: A five-minute account-level scan of weekly metrics to find the inflection point and which metric changed.
cards.use_when: When starting the Google Ads portion of a diagnosis, before looking at individual campaigns.

cards.title: Match failure modes to campaign type: PMax and Shopping
cards.summary: Why identifying the campaign type first matters, and the specific failure modes to check for PMax and Shopping.
cards.use_when: When a Google Ads decline has been traced to a specific campaign and you need to know what to inspect.

cards.title: Search campaign failure modes: search terms, auction insights, display leakage
cards.summary: Four specific checks for a declining Search campaign, including broad-match reallocation and display leakage.
cards.use_when: When diagnosis points to a Search campaign as the source of a performance decline.

cards.title: Metric decomposition: build the formulas before you touch anything
cards.summary: Every campaign KPI is the product of underlying metrics — learn the decomposition to reach the true root cause rather than the first visible symptom.
cards.use_when: When you've isolated a declining campaign metric and need to trace it down to the trigger that actually moved.

cards.title: CPC troubleshooting: quality score, competition and premium auctions
cards.summary: Three explanations for rising CPC and how to tell whether higher CPC is actually a problem.
cards.use_when: When diagnosing a Google Ads efficiency decline where cost per click has risen.

cards.title: Conversion-rate troubleshooting: tracking, landing page, audience, learning, offer
cards.summary: Five ordered causes of a website conversion rate drop on Google traffic.
cards.use_when: When the conversion-rate leg of the revenue equation has fallen and you need to find which factor is responsible.

cards.title: Volume troubleshooting: clicks = impressions × CTR, budget vs bid share loss
cards.summary: How to diagnose a loss of click volume, separating budget constraints from bid/quality constraints.
cards.use_when: When Google Ads efficiency is stable but volume (spend or revenue) has fallen and you need to find why clicks dropped.

cards.title: Competitive pricing scripts: pull products rather than match discounts
cards.summary: How a wholesaler used competitor price monitoring to avoid unprofitable Google Shopping auctions.
cards.use_when: When Google Shopping CTR and ROAS fall on specific products and you suspect a competitor has discounted the same items.

cards.title: Default to fixes, not rebuilds — and protect the learning phase
cards.summary: Apply targeted fixes and allow time to read them, because a rebuild resets learning and can worsen the decline.
cards.use_when: When you've reached the root cause and are choosing between a targeted change and restructuring the account.

cards.title: Isolate one fix at a time to preserve causal learning
cards.summary: Why applying multiple simultaneous fixes (the kitchen sink) prevents you from knowing what worked — and when to accept that trade-off.
cards.use_when: When deciding how many changes to apply to a landing page, offer or campaign after diagnosing a decline.

cards.title: Root-cause sentence test: don't touch the account until you can complete it
cards.summary: A gate before making any change — you must be able to state the metric, sub-metric, trigger and root cause in one sentence.
cards.use_when: Before applying any fix to a Google Ads account following a diagnostic process.

cards.title: Diagnose Whether You Are Overspending or Underspending on Google Ads
cards.summary: Google sits bottom-of-funnel and captures demand other channels create, so most accounts either over-invest or wrongly starve Google of budget.
cards.use_when: Setting annual or quarterly budget allocation across Google, Meta, TikTok and affiliates, or deciding whether to increase Google spend when the platform reports high ROAS.

cards.title: Consolidate Campaigns Before Segmenting Them
cards.summary: Campaigns learn in isolation, so splitting identical products across campaigns starves low-volume ones of conversion data and lowers ROAS.
cards.use_when: Auditing or restructuring campaign architecture (shopping, PMax, search) or when you see ROAS fall as you go down the campaign list.

cards.title: The Four Justifications for Segmenting a Google Ads Account
cards.summary: Only brand vs non-brand, geography, margin/efficiency targets and product category justify splitting campaigns beyond the consolidated default.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to create an additional campaign for a product line, market or margin tier.

cards.title: Convert SKAGs into Single-Topic Ad Groups
cards.summary: Responsive Search Ads need large impression pools to exit learning, so one-keyword ad groups should be replaced by themed groups of 10–20 keywords.
cards.use_when: Restructuring search campaign ad groups, or inheriting an account still running Single Keyword Ad Groups.

cards.title: Fix the Seven Most Common Google Ads Setup Mistakes
cards.summary: A rapid audit list of configuration errors that quietly drain budget or corrupt measurement in ecommerce accounts.
cards.use_when: Running an account audit or onboarding a store's existing Google Ads account.

cards.title: Set Up PMax Asset Groups with Matching Listing Groups
cards.summary: PMax's single biggest error is one default asset group or multiple asset groups that all share the same products.
cards.use_when: Building or auditing a Performance Max campaign for an ecommerce store.

cards.title: Use Brand Exclusions and Weigh What Actually Matters in PMax
cards.summary: Without brand exclusions a PMax campaign is effectively a retargeting campaign; the source ranks the variables that move PMax performance.
cards.use_when: Configuring or prioritising fixes inside an ecommerce PMax campaign.

cards.title: Run a Feed-Only PMax and Check Actual Channel Delivery
cards.summary: Test a feed-led retail PMax configuration against the store baseline without assuming strict audience or channel isolation.
cards.use_when: Evaluating a feed-led versus full-asset Performance Max campaign for an ecommerce product catalog.

cards.title: Use Max Conversion Value to Gather Data, Then Move to Target ROAS for Stability
cards.summary: Target ROAS does not raise average performance so much as flatten week-to-week volatility; Max Conversion Value makes bigger bets.
cards.use_when: Choosing or changing the bidding strategy on a PMax or shopping campaign.

cards.title: Build a Feeder Strategy: Cold Shopping Plus Warm PMax
cards.summary: A low-target-ROAS cold campaign reaches cheap auctions nobody else bids on, feeding a high-target-ROAS warm campaign that converts.
cards.use_when: Scaling cold new-customer acquisition on Google when PMax alone has plateaued and you suspect warm-traffic over-attribution.

cards.title: Recognise PMax's Ceiling and Reframe the Allocation Question
cards.summary: PMax is strong for smaller accounts but plateaus; the useful question is what percentage of spend goes to PMax versus standard shopping.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to keep scaling PMax or redistribute budget into standard shopping.

cards.title: Choose Between the Three Standard Shopping Structures
cards.summary: Top-seller split, feeder strategy and labelizer automation suit different catalogue sizes and business models.
cards.use_when: Choosing a standard shopping campaign structure for an ecommerce catalogue.

cards.title: Keep 80–90% of Ecommerce Google Spend in Shopping, Not Search
cards.summary: Shopping listings convey image, price, promos and comparison context pre-click, so they convert better than search ads in ecommerce.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to split budget between shopping and search campaigns for an ecommerce store.

cards.title: Choose Shopping vs Search by Buyer Type
cards.summary: Shopping captures most ecommerce leverage, but B2B-style bulk buyers on an ecommerce store often convert better through Search ads.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to split Google Ads budget between Shopping and Search when your store sells both to consumers and to businesses (bulk, wholesale, trade customers).

cards.title: Rebuild Google Shopping Product Titles for Keyword Reach
cards.summary: Structure Shopping feed titles around researched, converting search terms rather than internal product names, and generate variants from search term reports.
cards.use_when: Optimizing the Google Merchant Center feed so your product listings appear for more relevant search queries and earn more clicks.

cards.title: Diagnose and Break the Target ROAS Death Spiral
cards.summary: A target ROAS that keeps missing shrinks its own eligible audience until spend and conversions collapse, so reset the target aggressively when volume drops.
cards.use_when: Auditing a Google Ads account where spend has been gradually trailing off, or where target ROAS campaigns have stopped delivering volume.

cards.title: Pick Expansive vs Restrictive Bidding by Testing Appetite
cards.summary: Max conversion bidding spends ~30% of budget testing new audiences while target ROAS/CPA restrict auctions for efficiency, at the cost of siloing the account.
cards.use_when: Choosing or reviewing the bidding strategy for a Google Ads account and deciding whether you need scale discovery or tighter efficiency.

cards.title: Maximize Conversion Value Instead of Conversions for Mixed-Margin Catalogs
cards.summary: Optimizing for conversions pushes spend to cheap products with low CPAs, so value-based bidding better reflects where the profitable orders actually are.
cards.use_when: Choosing between maximize conversions/target CPA and maximize conversion value/target ROAS when your catalog spans very different price points and margins.

cards.title: Use Portfolio Bidding to Merge Learnings and Cap CPC
cards.summary: Account-level portfolio bid strategies let siloed campaigns share learning data and add max/min CPC limits on top of target ROAS or max value bidding.
cards.use_when: You have deliberately split campaigns into segments (brand, category, margin tiers) and want them to learn together, or you need to cap expensive clicks.

cards.title: Exploit Search Campaign Smart Bidding Exploration
cards.summary: Search campaigns can use a smart bidding exploration setting that lets target ROAS bid outside its target in 10-30% bands to keep discovering new auctions.
cards.use_when: You run Search campaigns on target ROAS and want some of the scale benefits of expansive bidding without abandoning efficiency targets.

cards.title: Build Negative Keyword Discipline in the First 30 Days
cards.summary: Search campaigns need heavy negative keyword review early because broad targeting bleeds spend, then lighter ongoing management to avoid resetting learnings.
cards.use_when: Launching or taking over Search campaigns and controlling wasted spend on irrelevant queries.

cards.title: Explain the Low Leverage of Average CPC
cards.summary: Average CPC is largely a vanity metric because traffic quality varies, so judge performance by conversion rate, AOV and ROAS instead.
cards.use_when: Reviewing Google Ads reporting or evaluating an agency's proposed CPC-focused optimization for your store.

cards.title: Win More Google Auctions by Raising Your Website's Conversion Rate
cards.summary: Because Google is an auction, a higher on-site conversion rate lets you afford higher bids than competitors and win more placements.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to invest to improve Google Ads performance when campaign settings have already been refined.

cards.title: Run Continuous Landing Page Split Tests on Search Ads
cards.summary: Duplicate ad groups with two ads pointing to two different landing pages, then rotate the winner against a new challenger every 30-60 days.
cards.use_when: Running Search campaigns and looking for the biggest lever beyond in-platform settings: improving the landing page conversion rate.

cards.title: Change Google Ads Budgets Slowly, Downward Faster
cards.summary: Google rewards slow methodical budget increases around 20%, and tolerates faster decreases, while other platforms allow quicker scaling.
cards.use_when: Scaling or pulling back spend on Google Ads campaigns after a winning period, or planning a promotion push.

cards.title: Interpret 'Limited by Budget' as a Signal, Not a Rule
cards.summary: The limited-by-budget flag appears on almost every account regardless of spend level, so treat it as a hint to investigate incremental spend rather than proof it exists.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to raise campaign budgets when Google Ads reports campaigns are limited by budget.

cards.title: Stagger Feed Title Rollouts to Protect Learning
cards.summary: Feed optimizations reset campaign learning, so roll title changes gradually and monitor CTR, CPC and returns in real time instead of switching everything at once.
cards.use_when: Applying Google Merchant Center title, image or attribute changes across a catalog with active Shopping and Pmax campaigns.

cards.title: Optimize Shopping Images for Contrast, Not Just CTR
cards.summary: Shopping images occupy about 70% of the listing, so design them to attract the right buyer through contrast with competitor listings rather than maximizing clicks from everyone.
cards.use_when: Improving Google Shopping listing creative to lift click quality, not just click volume.

cards.title: Set Up Separate Merchant Center Feeds per Currency
cards.summary: Running multiple regions through one feed forces Google to show live currency conversions, which damages CTR and conversion rate.
cards.use_when: Selling to international customers through Google Shopping and reviewing your Merchant Center feed setup.

cards.title: Audit Responsive Search Ads for Learning Starvation
cards.summary: RSAs have 2,700 asset combinations, so heavy segmentation keeps them permanently in learning and you should minimise segmentation to let them exit.
cards.use_when: Structuring Search campaigns and RSAs for an account with limited impression volume.

cards.title: Follow a 90-Day Google Ads Implementation Sequence
cards.summary: Roll out tracking, structure, Pmax checks, waste audits, asset health and slow feed changes in a deliberate order over roughly 90 days.
cards.use_when: Onboarding a new Google Ads account or planning a quarter of work on an existing ecommerce account.

cards.title: Exclude Brand Traffic and Use Smart Bidding on Search
cards.summary: Search campaigns should exclude brand terms and generally use a smart bidding strategy such as target ROAS or max conversions.
cards.use_when: Setting up or auditing Search campaigns in an ecommerce account.

cards.title: Your follower count no longer decides reach — the content graph does
cards.summary: Platforms now test every post on a small audience of strangers and expand distribution only if it performs, making follower count largely irrelevant to reach.
cards.use_when: Strategic decision about whether to invest in list building, follower growth tactics or raw content output for your store's organic social.

cards.title: Replace gallery-era polish with street-market speed
cards.summary: Over-produced brand content underperforms casual, fast, behind-the-scenes content under content-graph algorithms.
cards.use_when: Deciding the production style, budget and publishing cadence for a store's product or brand social content.

cards.title: Run the S.G.T.M.S. test loop on one concept at a time
cards.summary: A five-step cycle — Start one idea, Generate AI variations, Test fast, Measure deep metrics, Scale winners — turns content from guessing into a repeatable experiment loop.
cards.use_when: Setting up a weekly content test cycle for product discovery, ad creative or landing page hooks.

cards.title: Use AI as a pre-publish hook and pacing reviewer
cards.summary: Feed your script or transcript to an AI and ask it to grade the first three seconds, tighten captions and find slow drop-off points before you publish.
cards.use_when: Pre-publish review of a product video, Reel, ad hook or landing page headline.

cards.title: Reverse-engineer what the algorithm rewards before you publish
cards.summary: Platforms already score your content against top-performing patterns, so match those patterns before publishing rather than after it flops.
cards.use_when: Designing content for a new product launch or category where you do not yet know what performs.

cards.title: Turn repeatable formats into branded series instead of one-off experiments
cards.summary: Once a format consistently works, name it, stylize it, and rerun it as a series rather than chasing originality every post.
cards.use_when: Planning recurring content slots for your store, such as weekly tips, customer stories or product demos.

cards.title: Split content types into satellite accounts rather than one feed
cards.summary: Mixing tip content, product news and founder stories on one account confuses audience matching; separate accounts or clear content pillars keep signals clean.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to run multiple brand accounts or a single account with distinct content pillars for your store.

cards.title: Build a mid-funnel asset before asking for the sale
cards.summary: Viral top-of-funnel attention converts better when routed to a nurture asset (newsletter, waitlist, free trial) instead of a hard offer.
cards.use_when: Designing the path from an organic post or viral moment to a purchase for your store.

cards.title: Automate comment-to-DM capture to convert attention spikes into leads
cards.summary: Comment-triggered DM automation delivers lead magnets or booking links instantly, capturing interest before a viral moment cools off.
cards.use_when: Setting up response handling for a post, Reel or ad that may spike comments asking for a link, price or resource.

cards.title: Treat reach as a process, not luck: hook over history
cards.summary: Two operating rules for organic content — a single strong post can reset your reach, and consistency comes from repeatable formats, not chance.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to keep posting on an account with historically weak performance, or how to build a sustainable posting schedule.

cards.title: Format shakeup: graft proven entertainment structures onto dry topics
cards.summary: Steal a recognizable entertainment format and force a boring product or service topic into its exact structure to make organic content inherently watchable.
cards.use_when: Building a repeatable content series for a hardware, household, hobby or specialist product store.

cards.title: Speed as a content vehicle: compress the expected format
cards.summary: Doing a normally slow, ordinary demonstration at extreme speed turns routine business content into an event viewers and algorithms reward.
cards.use_when: Producing product demos, store tours, unboxings or process videos that are functionally fine but get no watch time.
